findings.title: Busy times are ignored on date-override days, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's date and the slot falls inside the override window, the code reaches `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (lines 133-135) and returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function is ever evaluated. `busy` contains the host's existing Cal.com bookings and external calendar events, so on any day that has a date override, none of the host's actual commitments block slots. This applies to fixed hosts in round-robin/collective events, to loose hosts (the loose-host loop calls the same function), and to personal events (whose single user counts as fixed). A host who already has a booking or calendar event inside an override window can be double-booked. The early return should only skip the working-hours check; the busy check must still run.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects every slot for hosts with multiple windows per day
findings.body: The new working-hours guard uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns `false` (slot unavailable) whenever the predicate matches ANY window in which the slot does not fit. Hosts commonly define split availability on a day, e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, which produces two WorkingHours entries with the same days. Any slot is necessarily outside at least one of those windows, so `find` always returns truthy and every slot is rejected. Because checkIfIsAvailable now runs for every fixed host (including the single user of a personal event, and both hosts of collective events), any event whose host has more than one availability window per day becomes completely unbookable on all days. The logic needs to be inverted: reject only when NO window for that day fully contains the slot (e.g. `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`).

findings.title: Working-hours check compares the window end against the slot start instead of the slot end
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is a copy-paste of the `start` computation; it should use `slotEndTime`. As written, `end > workingHour.endTime` only tests the slot's start time, so a slot that starts inside a window but finishes after the window closes (e.g. a 30-minute slot starting at 12:00 when the fixed host's window ends at 12:00, which can occur in round-robin/collective events where the slot originates from another host's hours) is treated as within working hours and can be booked past the host's availability.

findings.title: Multiple date-override windows on the same date break the availability check
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate returns true (causing the slot to be rejected with `return false`) for the first override on the matching date in which the slot is NOT contained, and find() stops iterating there. With two override windows on the same date (e.g. 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00), a slot at 14:30 is rejected because it is outside the first window, and a slot at 10:30 is rejected because it is outside the second window. Only a single override window per date works correctly. The check needs 'there exists an override on this date that contains the slot' semantics rather than short-circuiting on the first non-containing override.

findings.title: Override containment check treats partial overlap as available and misses the exact end boundary
findings.body: The conditions used to decide that a slot is outside an override are `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` and `slotStartTime > overrideEnd` (strict isAfter). Anything else — including a slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it — is treated as 'within the override' and the host is considered available, even though part of the slot falls outside the override window. Additionally, a slot starting exactly at the override end fails the strict `isAfter` and is also treated as inside the override. For round-robin events where slots are generated from other hosts' working hours, this lets fixed hosts be booked outside their override window. Availability should require full containment: slotStart >= overrideStart && slotEnd <= overrideEnd.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted date overrides that cross midnight are silently dropped
findings.body: The override start/end are shifted by (inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset) and then reduced to hour/minute-of-day via `.hour() * 60 + .minute()`. When the shift pushes the interval across midnight — e.g. a 09:00-17:00 IST override viewed from PST (offset -810 minutes shifts start to 19:30 of the previous day and end to 03:30) — the wrapped startTime (1170) becomes greater than endTime (210) whenever only one side of the interval wraps, and buildSlots silently skips the range (`if (start >= end) continue`). Meanwhile the user's regular working hours for that day were already spliced out of computedLocalAvailability, so the invitee sees the host as fully unavailable that day. Regular working hours handle midnight spanning by splitting the range; overrides need the same treatment.

findings.title: Zero-length override comparison uses === on dayjs objects and can never match
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')` compares two distinct dayjs object references, which is always false. The intended detection of zero-length overrides (a 'blocked' date override where start equals end) is dead code, so such overrides fall through to the boundary conditions instead of being explicitly excluded. Use `.isSame()` for the comparison.

findings.title: Override date matching is formatted in the server's local timezone but compared to a UTC date
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start)` creates a dayjs in the server machine's local timezone, and `.add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` is compared against `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')`, where slotStartTime is in UTC mode. On any host not running in UTC (self-hosted instances with a TZ set, dev machines), the two sides of the comparison are rendered in different zones, so an override can be matched against the wrong day near midnight. `dayjs.utc(date.start)` should be used so both sides are in UTC.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion silently depends on the server timezone when timeZone is absent
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is used to compute the organizer offset, but `timeZone` was added as an optional property on TimeRange, and dayjs.tz with an undefined zone falls back to the machine's local timezone. Any caller of getSlots that passes dateOverrides without a timeZone now gets results that depend on the server's timezone (and differ between UTC production servers and non-UTC dev machines), whereas the previous code did not consult a timezone at all. A deterministic fallback (e.g. `override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone`) should be used.

findings.title: No tests for the round-robin fixed-host scenario or for busy blocking on override days
findings.body: The PR adds only one test: a personal event viewed from a different timezone. The headline fix — date overrides of a fixed host constraining a round-robin event's slots — has no test. There is also no test that an existing booking or calendar busy time still blocks a slot on a date-override day (which would have caught the regression where the busy check is skipped when a date override matches), and no coverage for hosts with multiple working-hour windows in one day or multiple override windows on one date, both of which the new checkIfIsAvailable logic handles incorrectly.
